840	What have you got until now? Don't you see that HaShem
brought you this as a gift? Why are you getting so excited?
Why are you... "Wow, how I understood!" Say thank you to HaShem!
Where did you go? Where did you go to? A person does something
with money, succeeds in some business, and feels: "How
did I make this deal! What a... how talented I am!" Just a moment, Adonai,
do not forget. One can quietly go down to the lowest depths even
through the good, especially when a person gets carried away by his own power. Then
he acts above his level: "It's all me, it's all
my talent, all my strengths."
What a pity, this is...
>> Right, right.
>> What does it do? But that a good person, for whom everything seems
fine, must not get confused there.
>> That is why Rabbi Natan says, this is why we
go through all the ups and downs.
And our work is the work we received from Avraham
our father: to believe,
to believe that both the downs and the ups are all
from HaShem, for your good. Remember HaShem, remember HaShem,
says Rabbi Natan, because only for this was man created
and sent down to this physical world, full of husks and darkness,
so that he can bring out the very, very hidden kindnesses
from concealment into revelation.
This is the essence of the greatness of the Creator, blessed be He: the essence of the greatness
of the Creator is that man, in this world, reveals the great
mercies. Where?
In light and in darkness,
in tsedakah
and in mishpat, that he reveals the mercies,
that he reveals the hidden mercies.
This is the essence of the purpose of the descent for the sake of the ascent. For through
the descent
and nevertheless he strengthens himself — here is the advice: he strengthens
himself through faith
in His immense kindnesses, blessed be He, without end or limit. Through
this he reveals His kindnesses; he brings the hidden kindness
from concealment into revelation. And this is what is written about Avraham: "For
I have known him,
so that he may command his children and his household after him,
and they shall keep the way of HaShem, to do tsedakah and mishpat."
For this is the way of HaShem, that one surely does tsedakah and mishpat,
meaning that within the mishpat
he will do tsedakah, and within the tsedakah he will do mishpat. How is it possible
to understand this? It's confusing. You say, wait, I
don't understand. There is nothing to understand here: believe. Take this from the start
as an axiom, a basic premise: everything, everything is for your good.
The good is for your good. And if the good is withheld from you, it is
for your good. And if you have some difficulty, it is for your good.
>> In our relationship with the Holy One, blessed be He,
>> what we say... If I now, with my wife, with my daughter, a friend, should I also
read it like this, as "mishpat" wrapped in success? All of it, as I am saying now,
let me check: but you want to say something that is mishpat.
>> Yes. The answer is yes, but that is by itself,
because we need, as we are speaking here,
to believe
that everything is out of love, and that this is how HaShem leads the world,
with opposite attributes. >> This is actually Avraham's teaching: tsedakah within mishpat.
>> This is Avraham's teaching, and there is one more derivation
that I did not want to expand on, but it is definitely implied
here: it is also the way we must behave
with those close to us, with our wife, our children,
as our Sages said, or anyone I influence:
"Let the left hand always push away and the right hand draw close."
Tsedakah and mishpat is also a way of conducting life toward whoever
is before me. If I only do favors for whoever is before me,
he spits on me. He belittles me. He
doesn't appreciate anything, and in the end he becomes the poorest, because
he doesn't enjoy anything, since he doesn't know how
to appreciate anything. When we give to children, or
to people I work with, or anything like that,
we set boundaries and say "no," and we state
the din. There are rules, not everything is deserved. Then
when he receives, he knows how to appreciate, and then he enjoys,
and he merits a good life. And of course, if you only say "no,"
you have strangled the person.
So, so this too — you are completely right — is also a way
of conduct.
And here a lot is needed, as it were; the Holy One, blessed be He, knows
how to combine this, but with human beings, again,
if I only give, they don't know how to appreciate,
if I only close and withhold, they think
I am against them. Here too, a lot, a lot of siyata
diShmaya is needed. Let's see again, further on.
About this Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, asked: "Make me know
Your ways."
Moshe Rabbeinu says to HaShem: I don't understand how You,
how You lead the world. It's confusing, because You have
opposite attributes.
He asked to know the ways of HaShem, His judgments and His tsedakah.
He wants to understand the din in depth, I want to understand
the chesed in depth, and I want to understand the combination.
Who can understand this?
He wanted to grasp
how the Holy One, blessed be He, leads His world with tsedakah
and mishpat, so that he would know how to pray for Israel.
And it worked: HaShem, blessed be He, answered him and said, "I will cause
all My goodness to pass before you."
And He revealed to him all the 13 attributes of mercy.
And this is the level of "and they shall keep the way of HaShem, to do
tsedakah and mishpat," for keeping tsedakah and mishpat is
surely the way of HaShem.
And again, in a person's daily life,
there is the point of how I look at everything: everything
good is from HaShem. Thank You very much, I appreciate
it, I cherish it, I draw close to You, I
thank You, I am moved by You, because You give me
everything. And the bad, Heaven forbid, You know what You are doing,
it is for my good, it is because of love, not because
of hatred. You are not pushing me away, You are cleansing
me, and it is because You love me. And also with traits
and attributes I act in the world.
There comes a moment when I say, "Fine, there's no need to make such an effort,
there's no need
to advance, because after all, as we said about
Yishmael, everything is good." Remember that there is din, continue...
